findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed that the designated handwashing sink in the bar area was being used as a dump sink, despite facility procedure to use a separate bucket for waste bar liquids. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and educated staff about only using the handwashing sink for handwashing, and that the separate bucket should be used for waste bar liquids. An additional sign was placed above the handwashing sink. Ensure that handwashing sinks are not used for any other purposes other than handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed that a container of sausage gravy in the bottom part of the main prep cooler was measured at an internal temperature of 60 F. PIC stated that the sausage gravy had been recently put back in the cooler 30 minutes previously after being out for part of service. Inspector checked the internal temperature again 30 minutes later and the gravy was at 62 F. Inspector observes that all other items in the cooler are sufficiently cold holding at 41 F and below, and that the cooler has an ambient air temperature of 36 F. CORRECTED: PIC discarded the sausage gravy. Inspector and PIC discussed storing the sausage gravy, and other items that get cooled, in shallower pans so as to allow for more rapid cooling, and making sure staff are more aware of how long items are left on the counter. Ensure that TCS foods are maintained at temperatures of 41 F or less, and that items can cool quickly once placed in cold holding equipment.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer at the kitchen triple sink and the bar sanitizer bucket to be held at 100 ppm quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- sanitizer tablets were added and observed to be changed to 200 ppm. Ensure sanitizers are made and tested at a frequency to hold the sanitizing concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label (200-400 ppm for quaternary ammonia).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Inspector observed that the sliding cooler in the storage room to not contain an ambient thermometer. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) placed an ambient thermometer in the cooler.Ensure all cooling units holding temperature control for food safety (TCS) contain an ambient thermometer to monitor air temperatures at or below 41F.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a wet mop head stored in the basin of a mop bucket. The PIC was informed and will be reminding staff of appropriate mop storage. Ensure wet mops are placed in a position that allows for air drying to prevent the harborage of microorganisms with a high water activity.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed multiple cans (sliced stew tomatoes X5, pineapple chunks X1, and black olives X1) in dry storage to contain dents along the seams, or significant dents along the body. CORRECTED- inspectors discussed can denting and Botulism entry with the kitchen staff and person in charge (PIC). Regularly check for dents along the seams of cans, and for large dents throughout the body. Ensure dented cans are marked or separated from cans for service to be returned to food supplier.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspectors observed soda nozzles at the server station (Dr. Pepper, Diet Coke, Coke, and Mellow Yellow) to contain an accumulation of soil debris and a biofilm. CORRECTED- the soda nozzles were removed, and brought to the bar triple sink to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. The PIC found extra nozzles to switch out the current nozzles, for more frequent cleaning. Inspector and PIC discussed verifying cleaning methods for Coke equipment with supplier. These surfaces are considered food contact surfaces and could serve as a source of contamination.  Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of biofilms and soil debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspectors two opened containers of milk (2% in the kitchen cooler and chocolate at the bar) lacking date marking. Inspectors asked the PIC when the milks were opened. CORRECTED- the PIC was able to remember when the chocolate milk was opened and put the corresponding date on the container. PIC was unable to verify when the 2% was opened, and the milk was voluntarily discarded. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are date marked to be used or discarded within 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. [Pf]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed three wet sanitizer cloths on the bar counter and hanging from the sanitizer bucket. CORRECTED- the sanitizer cloths were moved to the sanitizer bucket. Wet sanitizer rags left out may allow for the growth and harborage of bacteria. Ensure wet sanitizer cloths are stored in a sanitizer bucket in between uses.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D). [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed two wet mop heads stored on the floor of the dry storage area. CORRECTED - PIC was informed and mop sticks were inverted to dry over the mop sink. Ensure wet mops are placed in a position that allows for air drying.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Multiple food contact surfaces were observed to contain an accumulation of soil debris and a biolfilm:
1) The back of the baffles of the ice machine.
2) Dr. Pepper, Diet Coke, Coke, Tea, and Mellow Yellow soda nozzles at the server station.
3) Soda nozzle at the bar.
4) Soda nozzle inlet at the bar.
CORRECTED- all of the items mentioned above were cleaned and sanitized. The ice baffles and soda nozzle inlet at the bar were wiped with a clean sanitation rag. The soda nozzles were taken to the triple sink to be washed and sanitized. These surfaces are considered food contact surfaces and could serve as a source of contamination.  Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of biofilms and soil debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Consumer advisory provided for raw/undercooked food.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no consumer advisory in the menu. A discussion occurred with the person in charge (PIC), and while most burgers are fully cooked, some customers do request to have their hamburgers not fully cooked. Inspector left consumer advisory guidelines with the PIC. The next time the menu is printed the facility must include a disclosure (using words such as “raw” or undercooked”, or an asterisk that leads to the reminder), and a reminder regarding the increased risk of food-borne illness associated with consuming undercooked animal proteins. Correct by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-603.11(C) Consumption of Animal Foods that are Raw, Undercooked, or Not Otherwise Processed to Eliminate Pathogens. (C) REMINDER shall include asterisking the animal-derived FOODS requiring DISCLOSURE to a footnote that states: (1) Regarding the safety of these items, written information is available upon request; (2) Consuming raw or undercooked MEATS, POULTRY, seafood, shellfish, or EGGS may increase your RISK of foodborne illness; or (3) Consuming raw or undercooked MEATS, POULTRY, seafood, shellfish, or EGGS may increase your RISK of foodborne illness, especially if you have certain medical conditions. [C]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a wet sanitizer rag on the bar counter at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- the sanitizer rag was moved to the sanitizer bucket. Wet sanitizer rags left out may allow for the growth and harborage of bacteria. Ensure wet sanitizer cloths are stored in a sanitizer bucket in between uses.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D). [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- Observed microwave above hot holding station to be soiled with food splash. CORRECTED- the PIC wiped the interior of the microwave with a wet sanitizer cloth. Nonfood contact surfaces that contain an accumulation of soil debris can allow for the contamination of ready to eat (RTE) foods. Ensure staff is cleaning non-food contact surfaces at a frequency that prevents food splash accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Observed no certified food manager to be present during inspection. Discussed with PIC, inspector recommended facility aqcuire multiple certified food managers to ensure one is present within facility. Ensure a certified food manager is present during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed microwave above hot holding station to be soiled with food splash. Discussed with PIC, microwave will be cleaned. Ensure staff is cleaning non food contact surfaces at a frequency that prevents food splash accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Two open gallons of milk (one white, one chocolate) were observed without date markings indicating when they were opened. PIC will discuss date marking with staff and, if open-dates cannot be determined for the milks, discard them. Ensure foods are labeled with the date prepared or opened, and used or discarded within 7 days.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date. (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food. [Pf]

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Single service spoons available to customers at the self-serve coffee station were observed stored mixed directions with handles and spoon-ends intermixed. Ensure utensils are presented to customers with handles out to prevent contamination of the food contact ends.
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Employees were observed three times washing hands then turning the faucet off without using a barrier. CORRECTED- Inspector discussed with PIC and employees. Ensure a paper towel (or other barrier) is used to turn the faucet off after washing hands.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The bar soda nozzle was observed heavily soiled with mold accumulation. CORRECTED- An employee disassembled, cleaned, and sanitized the soda nozzle. Ensure the soda nozzle is cleaned regularly to prevent soil accumulation.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: The bar 3 compartment sink and sanitizer bucket were observed with 100ppm quat. CORRECTED- Discussed with an employee, who had remade the sanitizer solution after lunch. After reviewing the sanitizer tablet labels, the employee adjusted the number of tablets to each sanitizer solution. The 3 compartment sink basin needs 3 tablets and the sanitizer bucket needs 2 tablets.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114 (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have a concentration based on manufacturer’s label (200-400ppm). [P]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Cheese sauce in a hot holding unit to the right of the cookline was observed at 116F (probed). A food employee had prepared the cheese sauce earlier in the day. Other foods in the hot holding unit were 135F or above. CORRECTED- The food employee reheated the cheese sauce on the stove to 165F.
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. [P]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Dead cockroaches were observed on glue traps and on the floor on the cookline, under dry storage shelves, and behind the bar. Dead cockroaches were also observed stuck to duct tape used to seal gaps between wall paneling to the left of the 3 compartment sink. See General Comments for details regarding pest control efforts. Clean facility to eliminate pest harborage and to aid in monitoring pest activity. Continue or increase pest control visits. Inspector will follow up in 30 days.
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Food debris and a dead cockroach was observed in the bottom of the bar beverage cooler (across from the walk-in cooler, where citrus is stored). Clean non-food contact surfaces as often as necessary to prevent soil accumulation.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Soil accumulation and food crumbs were observed behind the cookline equipment and under the dry storage shelves. Grease accumulation was observed on the fire suppression system to the right of the ventilation hood. Maintain physical facilities clean.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1) The ends of the microwave shelf are unsealed wood. Paint or otherwise seal the ends of the shelf so it is smooth and easily cleanable.
2) Coving is missing to the left of the vertical cooler, and to the left of the sink in the utility/mop room. Coving is not fully sealed to the wall in the corner to the right of the utility sink, and at the entrance of to the dry storage room.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Employees present have not completed food handler training. Ensure employees complete food handler training within 30 days of hire. Keep certificates available on file for review during inspections. Employees are in the process of completing food handler or food manager courses.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: No CFM was present at time of inspection. Ensure sufficient staff have completed CFM training to cover all shifts of food prep and service. (Previously observed 12/10/23.)
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Can opener observed soiled with debris accumulation. CORRECTED- The can opener was washed, rinsed, and sanitized upon inspector’s request. Clean the can opener after each use.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Foods in the 3 door cooler were observed out of temperature (probed). Some foods probed included (but not limited to) baked potatoes at 48F; baked beans at 47F; Italian beef at 50F; and pizza sauce at 47F. Most foods were 52F when probed (southwest potato salad, sliced cheese, gravy, sliced turkey, diced tomatoes, sliced ham, bacon, ham, and logs of hamburger). CORRECTED- All out of temperature TCS foods in the cooler were voluntarily discarded. 
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
The 3 door cooler is not holding foods at or below 41F. Foods in the cooler were 47-52F when probed. Foods were voluntarily discarded. PIC has called their repair technician. Inspector will follow up to see that the cooler is functioning properly.
4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
The back storm door is not tight-fitting. Daylight is visible around the edges and the door moves as the wind blows. Repair door so that it is tight-fitting or use the main back door.
6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent. [C]

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Leaks observed from the faucet at the utility sink. Repair faucets to eliminate the leaks. (Previously observed 12/10/23.)
5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; and (B) Maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Employees present have not completed food handler training. Ensure employees complete food handler training within 30 days of hire. Keep certificates available on file for review during inspections.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. [C]

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
No one present has completed allergen awareness training. CFMs must complete ANSI-approved allergen awareness training. Keep certificates available on file for review during inspections.
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
PIC could not provide a food manager certificate. PIC took the course at MCL through a previous employer and passed but did not receive a certificate. The registration is under the previous employer’s email. Ensure sufficient staff have completed CFM training to cover all shifts of food prep and service. Keep food manager certificates on file.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

Beans and two containers of Italian beef were observed without date markings. CORRECTED- Foods were labeled with the dates they were prepared. Ensure foods are labeled with the date they are opened or prepared.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date. (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food. [Pf]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Gaskets are damaged on the middle and right doors of the 3 door cooler. Replace gaskets so equipment is maintained in good repair.

5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; and (B) Maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Soil accumulation observed under shelving in the dry storage and under equipment throughout the kitchen. Maintain physical facilities clean.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

Soil accumulation observed under shelving in the dry storage and under equipment throughout the kitchen. Maintain physical facilities clean.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Lighting is not working at the end of the cookline above the small prep cooler and over the 3 compartment sink. Replace bulbs or repair lighting fixtures so the kitchen is well-lit.
6-303.11: The light intensity shall be at least a certain lux and present in certain areas. [C]

findings.comment:
No CFM present at time of inspection. Ensure sufficient staff have completed CFM training to cover all shifts of food prep and service.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

Can opener observed soiled with debris accumulation. CORRECTED- Large can opener is not typically used. Can opener washed, rinsed, and sanitized. If not used, maintain clean or remove from kitchen.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Open gallon of chocolate milk observed with a manufacturer use by date of 4/4. Chili and taco meat observed labeled with date markings of 4/4. All foods past date were voluntarily discarded.
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. [P]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Foods in the salad cooler had internal temperatures ranging from 43F (salsa in the bottom) to 49F (salsa and dressing portions in the top). Salad on the shelf just above the bottom was observed at 45F. The condensing unit in the top was blowing out cold air below 40F, but the hanging thermometer near the middle of the unit was observed holding at almost 50F. TCS foods on the top shelf and in the door were relocated to three door cooler, which was holding below 40F. GM adjusted the salad cooler thermostat to a colder setting and arranged product to potentially allow for more air circulation. Inspector will be back for a spot check in mid-November (see general comments for additional information).  
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Cook was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier prior to retrieving paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed, and proper handwashing technique poster is present for reference at the kitchen handwashing sink.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Proper use of restriction and exclusion
findings.citation_text:
2-201.11 GM was at the facility working in the office despite experiencing vomiting/diarrhea less than 12hrs prior. Inspector advised GM nobody should come to work sick even if tasks to be completed are only in the office. In the future, GM should contact owners to allow for proper coverage depending on duties that need to be conducted. Also, GM noted they used the employee restroom twice while on-site. Per inspector’s request, GM left the facility after disinfecting the employee restroom with bleach solution per the directions of the norovirus disinfection policy. GM shall not return to work at the facility until they have been symptom free at least 48hrs after no longer being symptomatic. 
The person in charge shall ensure that a food employee who who exhibits or reports a symptom, or who reports a diagnosed illness or a history of exposure as specified under Subparagraphs (A)(1) -(5) of this section is:
(1) excluded as specified under ¶¶ 2-201.12 (A) - (C), and Subparagraphs (D)(1), (E)(1), (F)(1), (G) or (H)(1) and in compliance with the provisions specified under ¶¶ 2-201.13(A) - (H); or
(2) restricted as specified under Subparagraphs 2-201.12 (D)(2), (E)(2), (F)(2), (H)(2), or ¶¶ 2-201.12(I) or (J) and in compliance with the provisions specified under ¶¶ 2-201.13(D) ­ (J). P 2-201.11:

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.citation_text:
3-403.11 Cheese sauce and chili being hot held in the same food warmer were observed with varying temperatures. Cheese sauce had internal temperatures ranging from 128F-145F, and chili had internal temperatures ranging from 120F-156F. Cheese sauce was prepared and heated on the stove using a commercially processed mix prior to placing in the warmer. Chili was a reheat from the day prior and was heated to ~145F prior to placing in the warmer, with the intent to finish the reheat to 165F. Both products were placed back on the stove and reheated to temperatures above 165F before hot holding. Ensure foods are at proper temperature throughout prior to hot holding. 
TCS food that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding shall be reheated so that all parts of the food reach a temperature of at least 165F for 15 seconds and done rapidly so the time the food is between 41F and 165F may not exceed 2 hrs.
Ready to eat, TCS food that has been commercially processed and packaged in a food processing plant that is inspected by the regulatory authority that has jurisdiction over the plant, shall be heated to a temperature of at least 135F when being reheated for hot holding.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14 Leftover portions of brown gravy, green beans, and corn were in covered containers cooling in the 3 door cooler. Internal temperatures were observed at 104F-109F for green beans, 95F-105F for corn, and 125F-134F for brown gravy. Manager noted the cook who was responsible for cooling the foods removed products from hot holding around 1:30pm. Ice baths are typically used to chill cooling foods prior to storing in the cooler. Foods in question were placed on an ice bath around 2:30pm in an attempt to quickly drop temperatures and reach 70F within 2hrs. Brown gravy had an internal temperature of 84F after 3:30pm and was discarded. Corn and green beans and internal temperatures at 68F-70F by 3:30pm and were kept in the ice bath to continue cooling prior to storage.
Ensure adequate ice baths are used and foods are cooled quickly/properly prior to storing items covered in the cooler. 
Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.
